note.text:
GenAI was pitched as the great equalizer — cheap intelligence for everyone, instantly. The data tells a different story.

Split a workforce by existing skill level and hand everyone the same GenAI tool. The already-skilled pull further ahead: they know what good output looks like, so they edit, challenge, and apply it fast. The less-skilled often stall, or worse, drift backward trusting flawed outputs they can't evaluate.

That's a K-shape, not a level-up. It matters because most adoption plans assume democratization is automatic — it isn't.

If judgment is the real bottleneck, access alone won't close any gap. Training people to evaluate AI output deserves as much budget as the AI license itself.

AI rewards those who already have the skills to judge it.
